summary:
SCOPE AND METHOD. Project root (PR) = C:/Users/Dario/OneDrive - Erasmushogeschool Brussel/Hackathon/Tectronic_30.09.2026/mirror. Read-only: no file under PR was modified (checked: nothing newer than 20:15 in backend/mirror, tests, moments, examples, data, web/src, .venv pyc; live WAL untouched, still 20:10:55). I never read .env.

The live DB CANNOT be copied. backend/data/mirror.duckdb and .wal are locked by the running uvicorn (python PID 35448, launcher PID 54084, started 20:07:34). bash cp gave 'Device or resource busy'; PowerShell FileShare.ReadWrite gave 'being used by another process'. So I regenerated the same dataset into the scratchpad. Generator run from a copy of the code in scratchpad/demo_verify/backend, so REPO_DIR has no .env. MIRROR_DB_PATH was pointed into the scratchpad, and the scripts assert that. Why this equals the live baseline: every source file is older than the live DB (code mtimes 19:23-19:55, DB 20:04:41); seed 42 is deterministic; fresh_gen.duckdb is 32,256,000 bytes, identical to the live file's size; two independent generations give identical events sums. The engine output was cross-checked by an independent pandas re-implementation of all 4 moments: max |inferred diff| 2.2e-16, identical row sets. All demo flows were replayed through the real FastAPI app via TestClient. Scripts and outputs: scratchpad/demo_verify/backend/v1..v11*.py and demo_verify/flow_out.txt. pytest: 22 passed (9-28 s here; README says ~5 s).

USERS (verified in DB plus real /api/auth/login for all six): sofie = customer 1 (Sofie, 31, Gent, lang en, advisor_id 1); lucas = customer 2 (27, Antwerpen, lang nl, advisor 2); marc = customer 3 (44, Liège, lang fr, vulnerable=true, advisor 1); an = advisor_id 1 (An Peeters); jan = advisor_id 2 (Jan Claes); po = product_owner, no links. generate.py:249-299, 350-357.

NO-KEYS BEHAVIOUR (simulated: GEMINI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT and ELEVENLABS_API_KEY empty, no .env). Everything works. Every intro is written_by='template' (channels.py:70-71 returns None without a key). Templates are in the customer's language, e.g. 'Hallo Sofie, hier is één plan voor dit moment...'. Pressing Listen (Mirror.tsx:213-229, 266-270): the button reads '▶ Listen' (NL '▶ Beluisteren'), shows '▶ …' while the request runs, then a small muted line under the buttons reads exactly: 'Voice channel not configured (set ELEVENLABS_API_KEY)'. That is the 503 detail from api.py:316-317, always in English even in the NL UI. No audio and no toast. Listen on a rejected moment gives 404 'No active guidance for this moment'. More than 6 presses per minute gives 429 'Too many requests, slow down' (security.py:101). The 'Intro written by AI' note (Mirror.tsx:271) never appears, so the 'AI writes the words' claim cannot be shown on stage without a Gemini key. With a bad or unreachable voice key the user sees 'Voice service unavailable' (502). A working ElevenLabs or Gemini path is untested; the README admits this. Whether .env holds keys is unknown (not read). Weak hint only: .env is 1,091 bytes vs 1,012 for .env.example, i.e. +79 bytes, roughly room for a 64-char JWT secret plus a short password and no API keys.

LIVE DB STATE (inference only, file unreadable). mirror.duckdb is still 32,256,000 bytes with mtime 20:04:41, so no checkpoint has happened since generation; everything since lives in the WAL. The WAL is 14,424,154 bytes, last write 20:10:55, idle since. Measured WAL sizes in scratch: startup run 7.12 MB; startup plus one more full run 14.24 MB; startup plus add EV plus run 14.90 MB. The live WAL is 14.24 MB plus about 180 KB, and one feedback write plus refresh is about 20 KB. Most likely there has been at least one extra 'Run on all customers' after startup plus a handful of small mutations (feedback, consent, language or cache writes). Treat the live DB as dirty. The API also showed in the working set that uvicorn is paged out to 2 MB. Possible distortions, all of which a reset removes:
- leftover feedback: Sofie already confirmed or rejected, Marc confirmed;
- a practiced 'ev_purchase' custom moment: PO table shows a 'new' row and 'Validate & go live' returns 409 'a moment with id ev_purchase already exists';
- customers.language of Sofie left at NL and consent toggles left off;
- cached intros (finding 5);
- last run stats in runs, which is what the PO first screen shows.

RESET PROCEDURE (recommended, full; generation is deterministic so all numbers above recur).
0. Free RAM (only 0.67 of 15.2 GB free now; close Edge, ChatGPT and the like), plug in, power plan is 'Balanced'. The project sits inside OneDrive (OneDrive has used 3,386 CPU-s); either pause sync or set MIRROR_DB_PATH to a non-synced folder for BOTH generator and uvicorn.
1. STOP the API first. Ctrl+C in the uvicorn terminal, or 'taskkill /PID 54084 /T /F' (launcher plus child). Leave Vite on 5173 running. A clean stop removes mirror.duckdb.wal; a force-kill leaves the WAL, which is harmless because the generator deletes it.
2. cd backend; .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m mirror.generate --customers 100000. It takes 10-25 s and prints {'customers': 100000, 'events': 6116388, 'planted_moments': 5436, 'advisors': 50, ...}. DEMO_PASSWORD is read from .env by config (tested with a scratch .env). If the output contains 'Demo password for all demo users', DEMO_PASSWORD was not set and the password changed.
3. .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m uvicorn mirror.api:app --port 8000 (same command as now). Wait 2-6 s for startup; it builds twin and signal_hits and the first runs row (engine.py:38-39).
4. Check without clicking through the demo: po shows 4 moments, none tagged 'new', events 6,116,388. sofie: two 'We're asking you' cards, 82% and 55%, language EN, no Undo buttons. marc: 'With your advisor'. lucas: Dutch plan. an: Marc first with 'needs you', Sofie about 5th. Do not rehearse the flow afterwards or repeat the reset.
LIGHTER ALTERNATIVE, tested on a dirty scratch copy (feedback, EV, NL, consents off, cache filled): with the API STOPPED, run in backend with the venv python: DELETE FROM feedback, custom_moments, message_cache, runs; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS twin, signal_hits; UPDATE customers SET language (1 'en', 2 'nl', 3 'fr'), consent_transactions=true, consent_app=true WHERE customer_id IN (1,2,3); then start the API. EXCEPT ALL comparison against a fresh generation showed 0 differences on customers, twin, signal_hits, feedback, custom_moments, message_cache, moments_rt, truth and meta.
DO NOT run the generator while uvicorn is up (finding 1). In-app undo (Remove EV, Undo clicks) is incomplete: it leaves message_cache, runs and the ev_purchase feedback row (finding 6).

findings.title: Generator silently 'succeeds' while the API is running: the server keeps serving the old deleted DB
findings.detail: The README reset instruction is 'stop the API and run the generator again' (README:74), but nothing enforces it. generate() unlinks mirror.duckdb and .wal (lines 317-320) and writes a new file. On this Windows 11 box DuckDB holds the file with delete-sharing, so the unlink succeeds and the generator exits 0 while uvicorn keeps serving the orphaned old file. The UI then looks un-reset. Yet the same lock blocks reading the file (cp and PowerShell FileShare both fail).
findings.evidence: Scratch test (v6/locktest): process A held a 200-customer DB open; process B ran 'python -m mirror.generate --customers 300' on the same path -> exit code 0, no error. A kept answering count(customers)=200 for the next 14 s and could still UPDATE; the file at the path then had 300 customers. Live file copy attempts: bash 'Device or resource busy', PowerShell 'being used by another process'.
findings.fix: Stop uvicorn (Ctrl+C or taskkill /PID 54084 /T /F), confirm the WAL is gone, then run the generator, then start uvicorn. Optionally make generate.py fail if duckdb.connect on the existing path cannot take the lock before unlinking.
findings.demo_impact: If you reset under time pressure without stopping the API, sofie/marc/EV state from practice is still on screen although the generator printed success.

reasons:
The behaviour reproduces, but it is a documented operator footgun and not a demo-breaking bug, so severity should be lower than high. Nothing in the code prevents or detects it. generate.py:317-320 unlinks mirror.duckdb and .wal with no lock or liveness check, and db.py:28 is a plain duckdb.connect. api.py:47-49 opens the DB once at startup and holds that connection for the life of the process. There is no reset endpoint or re-open logic.

I reproduced it in scratch copies only, on this Windows 11 box with duckdb 1.5.6. I did not touch the real DB.
- Run 1: process A held a 200-customer DB open, and `python -m mirror.generate --customers 300` ran against the same MIRROR_DB_PATH. The generator printed its success stats dict. A then returned count(customers)=200 at t=3, 6, 9 and 12 s.
- Run 2: I captured the exit code directly and it was 0. A still saw 200 customers and its INSERT into feedback succeeded after the regenerate. On a fresh reopen the file at the path had customers=300 and feedback=0. A's write did not corrupt the new file and left no stray .wal, so the only effect is stale state on screen.

Why it is lower than high:
- README.md:74 tells the operator to stop the API before regenerating, so the trigger is skipping a documented step.
- The effect is a visibly stale UI, not a crash, data loss or corruption. It is fixed by restarting uvicorn, which takes a few seconds.
- The data is synthetic.

The mitigation is operational: stop uvicorn, run the generator, start uvicorn. An optional hardening would be to make generate() try an exclusive duckdb.connect on the existing path before unlinking.

I am treating the demo_impact claim (practice sofie/marc/EV state stays on screen after a reset under pressure) as plausible, since Run 1 and Run 2 show a live server keeps serving the old data, but I did not test against the real server. The scratch files are in `C:/Users/Dario/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Dario-OneDrive---Erasmushogeschool-Brussel-Hackathon-Tectronic-30-09-2026/3b438afa-ea49-4084-a20d-604844ed0009/scratchpad/refute_lock`.

Reproduced, but "high" is overstated. The defect is a documented-procedure footgun with a one-step recovery, and it does not touch any demo code path.

What I read and ran:
- backend/mirror/generate.py:317-320 unlinks mirror.duckdb and .wal with no lock check. Line 321 then opens a new DB. main() (line 389) just prints the stats dict, so exit code 0 and an empty stderr look like success.
- backend/mirror/api.py:46-49 (lifespan) opens one DB(config.DB_PATH) connection per process and keeps it until shutdown. That is the handle that keeps serving the old file.
- Direct test: process A held a 200-customer scratch DB open (scratchpad/v7lock/holder.py). While A held it, a second process could not open the same file even read-only ("IO Error: Cannot open file ..."). Running `python -m mirror.generate --customers 300` on the same path via MIRROR_DB_PATH exited 0. A kept answering count(customers)=200 and kept accepting UPDATEs for another ~35 s. After A exited, the file at the path had 300 customers.
- End-to-end test with a real uvicorn on scratch port 18999 and a scratch DB (scratchpad/v7e2e/e2e.py). I logged in as sofie and PUT /api/me/consents to false/false. I then ran the generator with the API still up: exit 0, empty stderr. GET /api/me/twin still returned consents false/false, where a fresh DB gives true/true. After I killed the server, the file at the path held 300 customers with sofie at (True, True). So the new file is correct and nothing clobbers it on shutdown. Only the running process is stale.

Why I downgraded it:
- README.md:74 already says to stop the API before regenerating. The finding needs the operator to skip that step and also skip restarting the API.
- Recovery is seconds: restart uvicorn. The orphan file disappears when the old process exits, and nothing is corrupted.
- The effect is visible right away as a UI that did not reset. It does not affect the algorithm, visualisation, auth or any normal demo path.
- There is a real footgun from the silent exit 0 with no warning. The optional fix is feasible: a duckdb.connect on the existing path fails with an IO error while the server holds it, so a pre-unlink guard in generate.py would catch it. It is worth a small guard, but it is not a demo blocker.

Two points from the finding I did not check: the cp and PowerShell copy failures on the live file, and the Windows-specific delete-sharing explanation. The DuckDB open failing while the file is held is the part that matters for the fix.

Scratch processes are gone and nothing was written inside the project root.

findings.title: Live DB state is unverifiable and most likely dirty (practice leftovers)
findings.detail: The running server holds an exclusive lock, so feedback, custom_moments, message_cache and runs could not be inspected. File metadata shows writes since generation: the .duckdb is unchanged at 32,256,000 bytes, mtime 20:04:41 (no checkpoint since), while the WAL is 14,424,154 bytes, last write 20:10:55, server started 20:07:34, idle since. Scratch WAL fingerprints: startup run = 7.12 MB, startup + one more run = 14.24 MB, startup + EV add + run = 14.90 MB. Live = 14.24 MB + ~180 KB, i.e. at least one extra full population run plus roughly 9 small feedback/refresh-type writes. The live python process working set is 2 MB (peak 322 MB), so the first request after idle will be slow.
findings.evidence: ls --time-style=full-iso of backend/data; v8_wal.py and v9_wal_ev.py outputs (7,120,769 / 14,260,645 / 14,896,905 / 14,240,535); Get-Process -Id 35448 WS 2 MB.
findings.fix: Do the full reset procedure in the summary before going on stage. To inspect instead of resetting: stop the API, then open the DB read-only with .venv python and SELECT from feedback, custom_moments, message_cache, runs.
findings.demo_impact: A leftover ev_purchase moment makes 'Validate & go live' return 409 and pre-fills the PO table; leftover feedback makes Sofie start already confirmed/rejected, so the 'asks, not assumes' moment is gone; Sofie left in NL makes the language switch invisible.

reasons:
The core observation holds, but it is a pre-demo hygiene item rather than a defect, and two of the stated demo impacts are refuted or unlikely.

CONFIRMED
- I could not inspect the live DB. `cp` of both `backend/data/mirror.duckdb` and `mirror.duckdb.wal` fails with "Device or resource busy" while PID 35448 (started 20:07:34) runs.
- The file metadata matches the finding. `.duckdb` is 32,256,000 bytes, mtime 20:04:41. The WAL is 14,424,154 bytes, mtime 20:10:55. Both were still unchanged at 21:03. So all writes happened before this workflow began at 20:16, and no reviewer dirtied the live DB.
- Startup only runs `run_population()` when `twin` is absent (engine.py:38-39), and generate.py creates no `twin` (generate.py:327-363). So the first server start writes one full run.
- I reproduced the WAL arithmetic on a scratch copy of a fresh DB, using a copy of the code in `scratchpad/rf_inspect/backend`:
  - Startup alone gives 7,120,7xx bytes.
  - Startup plus one extra run gives 14,240,4xx.
  - Adding nine `refresh_customer` calls on demo customers (feedback or consent) gives 14,423,287, or 14,422,491 for refresh only. Live is 14,424,154, which is 0.9 to 1.7 KB higher, room for a few 136 to 330 byte writes.
  - One refresh on a customer with twin rows costs about 20.2 KB. Language UPDATE costs 136 B and a `message_cache` insert 330 B.
- So at least one extra population run and about nine feedback or consent writes happened between 20:07 and 20:11. The reviewer's "small writes" wording is wrong (about 20 KB each), but the count is right. The net state is still unknown; some of those writes could have been undone.

REFUTED OR OVERSTATED
1. A leftover `ev_purchase` moment causing a 409 is very unlikely.
   - Startup, EV add and run gives 14,896,826 bytes, which does not match live.
   - An EV add without a run costs 3,799 B, which does not fit the residual.
   - Any further run crosses the 16 MB auto-checkpoint. I saw the DB mtime change in scratch mode E, and the live mtime did not change.
   - Even if it were present, the PO table has a "Remove" button (ProductOwner.tsx:190-195, 60-67 -> api.py:422-427 -> engine.py:75-83). In scratch, the second add raised "already exists" (the 409 path, api.py:416-418), removal returned True, and re-adding worked.
2. Leftover feedback is plausible but recoverable in one click per belief. The "Undo" button is at Mirror.tsx:181-184 and sends the `clear` action (api.py:225-227). In scratch, confirming and rejecting feedback for customers 1 to 3 and then clearing it restored `twin` and `signal_hits` for those customers exactly, with 0 feedback rows left.
3. Language is a one-click EN/NL/FR switch (Mirror.tsx:56-66), and Sofie is seeded `en` (generate.py:252). A leftover NL is fixed before starting.
4. "First request after idle will be slow" is refuted.
   - `/api/health` on the live server answered in 39 ms cold and 11 to 13 ms warm.
   - In scratch I trimmed a DuckDB process from 196 MB to 7 MB working set, matching the live idle state. Three customer reads took 34 ms against 18 ms warm, and the full population run was unchanged (2.67 s against 2.61 s on a loaded machine).
5. A documented reset already exists. README.md:74 says to stop the API and rerun the generator. generate.py:317-320 deletes the `.duckdb` and `.wal` before regenerating.

VERDICT
Real as an operational caution: the live DB has been mutated since generation, so stop the API and regenerate, or clear feedback, consents and language via the UI, before the demo. It is low severity, not high, because it is not a code defect, it is fixed in under a minute, and the worst-case demo impact is undoable in the UI.

All scratch experiments are in `C:/Users/Dario/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Dario-OneDrive---Erasmushogeschool-Brussel-Hackathon-Tectronic-30-09-2026/3b438afa-ea49-4084-a20d-604844ed0009/scratchpad/rf_inspect/backend` (walexp.py, opdelta.py, trim.py, roundtrip.py).

VALID, with one correction: the leftover-EV/409 scenario is ruled out; the leftover-feedback and language scenarios stay plausible but cannot be confirmed from outside. The stated severity (high) still holds, because the core risk is real and likely.

1. Unverifiable. The live files are locked by the uvicorn server (pid 35448, started 20:07:34 from the user's VS Code pwsh). `cp` returned "Device or resource busy", and a .NET open with FileShare.ReadWrite,Delete gave a sharing violation on both mirror.duckdb and mirror.duckdb.wal. I could not copy or query the live feedback, custom_moments, message_cache or runs tables. The user's uvicorn access log is in their VS Code terminal, which the Terminal panel tool does not show. I did not stop the server or read .env.

2. The files match the reviewer's metadata. mirror.duckdb is 32,256,000 bytes with mtime 20:04:41 (no checkpoint since generation). mirror.duckdb.wal is 14,424,154 bytes with mtime 20:10:55, unchanged about 50 minutes later.

3. WAL reproduction. I replayed the real code (byte-identical scratch copy of backend/mirror) on a fresh-generation copy and got these sizes.
   - Startup (Engine.__init__ runs a full population because generate.py:363-372 never creates twin or signal_hits; engine.py:38-39): 7,120,811 bytes.
   - One POST /api/po/run (engine.py:91-104): +7,119,803 bytes.
   - Any feedback confirm, reject or undo, or any consent toggle (api.py:218-235, 244-253, engine.py:106-116): +19.8 to 20.4 KB each.
   - Language change or a guidance load: +136 to 766 bytes.
   
   Live 14,424,154 minus 7,120,811 minus 7,119,803 leaves 183,540 bytes, which is about 9 refresh-type writes. So after server start there was at least one extra full "Run on all customers" plus roughly 9 feedback or consent writes. The WAL is under DuckDB's 16 MB auto-checkpoint size, so none of this reached the .duckdb file.

4. Why "most likely dirty" is only an inference. The UI has an Undo button that also issues a ~20 KB write (Mirror.tsx:182, api.py:225-227), so the writes could net to zero. Feedback rows, consents and language are all persisted (db.py:62-93, api.py:261-266), and message_cache is written even for template text (channels.py:145-149). The finding omits that consent toggles look identical in the WAL.

5. Demo impact check on a scratch copy (/…/scratchpad/dbrepro/impact.py).
   - Fresh: Sofie is in EN, buying_home is 82% "ask" and growing_family is 54% "ask".
   - After one normal rehearsal of her scene, left as-is: Sofie is in NL, buying_home is 100% "act" with feedback "confirmed", and growing_family is 0% "suppressed_feedback". The "asks, not assumes" and "Not true" moments are gone (dsl.py:213, 224).

6. The leftover-EV claim (409, pre-filled PO table) is contradicted by the reviewer's own numbers. Adding the EV moment through the UI is always POST then run (ProductOwner.tsx:51-53). I measured EV add plus run at +7.77 MB after startup, while the live WAL has only 7.30 MB after startup. A duplicate add does return 409 (api.py:412-418), but the WAL size means EV was not run. It could only exist if added by direct API call with no run, which is unlikely.

7. "First request after idle is slow" is confirmed but confounded. The live server has 806 MB private memory and a ~2 MB working set. A cold GET /api/health took 11,136 ms; the next two took 459 ms and 14 ms. Free RAM was only 364 MB of 15.5 GB because other review agents were running, so a clean demo machine would be milder. It does not touch the DB, so a DB endpoint could be slower.

8. Fix: stop the API, run `python -m mirror.generate --customers 100000` (README, "To regenerate a clean demo state"), restart, then log in as sofie and check she is in EN with both beliefs "ask". A plain restart keeps the dirty state, because the WAL is replayed. This is a pre-stage checklist item rather than a code bug, which is why the impact is conditional even though the likelihood is high.

findings.title: 'Under a second' run time is not reproducible here: 1.7 to 9.6 s, and the UI prints the real number
findings.detail: README:103 and README:119 claim under a second / 0.6-1 s. ProductOwner.tsx:87-88 and :102 render stats.run_ms in ms next to that narrative. Measured on this machine now: startup run 1,691-2,193 ms; repeated 'Run on all customers' 2,602 / 4,307 / 4,158 / 9,571 / 2,828 / 3,821 ms; standalone 2,639-4,904 ms; EV add + run 2,777 to 9,450 ms. Wall 3.9 s vs only 1.6 s process CPU, so it is waiting (memory/IO), not compute-bound. Free RAM 0.67 of 15.2 GB, CPU load 29-31%, Defender and OneDrive active, power plan Balanced. Profile: pure SELECT of the hit query 264-320 ms; CTAS of signal_hits 0.8-2.0 s; CTAS of twin 1.1-2.0 s. run_population holds db.lock for the whole run (lines 96-104), so every other API call, including logins, blocks meanwhile.
findings.evidence: v2_flow.py 2b output; v3_bench.py warm run_ms [2639, 4492, 2837, 3097, 4630, 3669, 4634, 4904]; v4/v5 profiling; v10_jan.py 'wall 4014 ms, process CPU 1593 ms'.
findings.fix: Before the demo: close memory-heavy apps, plug in, set high-performance power plan, pause OneDrive, press 'Run on all customers' once to warm up, and say 'a couple of seconds' or quote the number on screen instead of 'under a second'. If the claim is kept, re-measure on the demo machine after the reset.
findings.demo_impact: The on-screen KPI 'Run time 2,639 ms' (or more) contradicts the spoken claim in front of the judges, and the UI appears frozen for up to ~9 s during the EV add.

reasons:
The core claim reproduces, but "high" overstates it and two of its side claims are weak.

Confirmed:
- README.md:17, :102 and :119 say "under a second" and "0.6 to 1 s". The only place the UI shows a number is the real `run_ms` (ProductOwner.tsx:87 and :102). `run_ms` is timed in engine.py:91-100, before `stats()` runs, so it is an honest figure.
- I generated a fresh 100k-customer DB (6,116,388 events, matching README:43) in my scratchpad. I did not touch the live DB.
- I timed `Engine.run_population` with the venv Python 3.14.5 and duckdb 1.5.6. Across about 60 runs I never got under 1 s. The first run on a fresh DB took 1,290 ms. Warm runs took 1.4 to 3.3 s typically, with some at 4.4 to 5.3 s and one at 20.9 s.
- Adding the EV moment and running took 2.1 to 4.9 s wall, median 3.8 s (run_ms 1.95 to 4.7 s). Reach 434, precision 0.998 and recall 0.265 match README.
- `run_population` holds `db.lock` for the whole run (engine.py:96-104). `login` calls `state.db.one` (api.py:158), which takes the same lock (db.py:35-41), so it would wait during a run. The reviewer's numbers are therefore in the right range.

Why "high" is too strong:
- The UI itself makes no "under a second" claim. The mismatch is only between the README or spoken script and an honest on-screen number of roughly 1.3 to 4 s. A wording fix is enough: quote the on-screen number, or say "a couple of seconds".
- README.md:119 scopes the 0.6 to 1 s figure to "our test environment". Only :17 and :102 are unscoped.
- My runs happened while the machine was heavily loaded, at 40 to 99% system busy. MsMpEng (Defender) was at about 240% CPU, OneDrive at about 110%, and dozens of claude, python, node and msedge processes were running, most of them from this review workflow. Available RAM was 0.0 to 1.9 GB of 15.2 GB. The machine was on AC power at about 4.0 GHz, so it was not throttled.
- Some runs were clearly waiting rather than computing, which supports the reviewer's memory diagnosis. One run had 5.5 s wall against 1.6 s CPU at 17% system busy. Another had 21.9 s wall against 2.5 s CPU at 0.00 GB available. Other runs showed CPU above wall (4 to 5 s CPU, 2 to 3 s wall), so the run is also multi-threaded and compute-heavy, not purely waiting.
- A run needs only about 0.25 to 0.3 GB resident (peak working set 0.24 to 0.28 GB). The slowdown comes from system-wide memory starvation, not from the engine.
- The `twin` CTAS is the dominant step, about 1.5 to 2.2 s. Writing it to a TEMP table still took about 1.7 s, so most of it is compute under contention, not the disk write the finding implies. The hit query SELECT is about 0.3 to 0.4 s.
- The demo machine will be quieter once the review agents stop, so an idle figure under 2 s is likely. I could not verify an idle figure under 1 s, so the README number remains unproven.

"UI appears frozen for up to ~9 s" is overstated:
- The run button shows "Running…" and is disabled (ProductOwner.tsx:91-93).
- The EV flow sets "Running it on every customer…" (:52), and "Validate & go live" is disabled while running (:212).
- api.ts:24-31 has no fetch timeout, so a slow run just completes.
- Blocking logins is irrelevant for a single presenter.
- The rate limit of 6 runs per 60 s (security.py:102) is not hit by the demo flow.

One citation is off by one: the "under a second" demo-script line is README.md:102, not :103.

REPRODUCED, but it is a wording and credibility risk, not a functional bug, so I rate it medium rather than high.

Code facts (read):
- README.md:102 says "100k customers, 6.1M events, under a second". README.md:119 says "A full run takes 0.6 to 1 s in our test environment". README.md:17 also says "under a second". The finding cites :103 for the first, which is actually :102.
- engine.py:91-104: run_ms is the time for two full CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE statements (signal_hits, twin) and is stored under db.lock.
- ProductOwner.tsx:87 and :102 print stats.run_ms in ms next to the narrative. The UI shows the real number and does not fake it. During a run the button reads "Running…" and is disabled (ProductOwner.tsx:91-92), so it is not literally frozen.
- api.py:430-433 (po_run) calls run_population directly. The DB wrapper uses one RLock (db.py), so every other DB call waits for the run.

Commands run (scratch copy of a 100k/6.1M DB in scratchpad/v20, scripts bench.py, bench2.py, bench3.py; the live mirror.duckdb is locked by the server on :8000, so I used an earlier scratch copy). Free RAM was ~0.6-1.6 GB of 15.9 GB, the power plan was Balanced, and the CPU was shared with other review agents, so timings are noisy:
- Population run_ms over 10 runs: 1298, 2301, 2541, 2977, 2385, 2689, 2654, 2929, 2804, 2968. Median 2.67 s, 0 of 10 under 1,000 ms.
- EV add + run, as the UI does it: add_custom takes 25-53 ms, run_ms was 1789, 2534, 2929, 2856 and 3445 (wall 2.0-3.6 s).
- CTAS stage split: signal_hits 0.7-2.1 s, twin 2.5-3.2 s.
- Lock blocking is confirmed: a trivial SELECT 1 issued 150 ms into a run waited 3,229 ms.
- Outliers are worse than the finding's 9.6 s. Separately, run_ms was 15,682 ms and 5,122 ms on a later run. Shared-machine load may have contributed, but the variance is real.

Corrections to the finding:
- The suggested "press Run once to warm up" does not help. In my data the first run is the fastest (1.3-1.7 s) and later runs are slower (2.3-3.4 s, with spikes), matching the reviewer's own startup-vs-warm numbers. An explicit CHECKPOINT between runs did not help (2.9, 3.4, 15.7, 5.1 s).
- "UI appears frozen" is overstated. The UI shows "Running…", but logins and persona switches issued during the run really do block.

Why medium, not high: the demo still processes 100k customers and 6.1M events in about 2-3 s, and the KPI shows the true number. The damage is the mismatch between "under a second" (README:17/102/119 and the spoken script) and the on-screen ~2,600 ms, plus the risk of a long stall at the 0:20 and 2:15 steps. The fix costs a few words: say "a couple of seconds" or quote the on-screen number, change README lines 17, 102 and 119, and don't switch personas while a run is in flight. Also check the demo laptop has free RAM and that the database file lives outside the OneDrive sync folder (currently it is inside it).

findings.title: Cached intro text is not invalidated when consent changes, so withdrawn evidence is still named
findings.detail: message_cache is keyed by (customer, moment, state, lang, channel) and not by evidence. The consent endpoint (api.py:244-253) refreshes beliefs but leaves the cache, so the guidance intro keeps quoting data the customer switched off, while the 'why' field is live.
findings.evidence: v2_flow step 7: Sofie (state ask) intro 'based on a transfer to a notary and a mortgage simulation in the app'. After PUT /api/me/consents app=false: belief evidence is only 'a transfer to a notary' (0.64, still ask) but guidance intro is unchanged and still mentions 'a mortgage simulation in the app', while why = 'a transfer to a notary'.
findings.fix: Add an evidence hash to the cache key, or DELETE FROM message_cache WHERE customer_id=$cid in refresh_customer.
findings.demo_impact: Not in the 3-minute script, but a judge toggling 'How you use the app' sees the text contradict the UI promise 'Off means we don't read it at all' (i18n.ts dataNote).

reasons:
Confirmed by code and by a run on a scratch DB. The bug is real as stated.

Code:
- `channels.py:127-150` (`Channels.intro`) caches by `(customer_id, moment_id, state, lang, channel)`. The key is built at line 128 and the `message_cache` primary key is at `db.py:91`. Evidence is not part of the key. A hit returns the stored text at lines 129-131 without looking at the current labels.
- Nothing ever deletes from `message_cache`. A grep of `backend/mirror` shows only the SELECT at `channels.py:122` and the INSERT OR REPLACE at `channels.py:146`.
- `PUT /api/me/consents` (`api.py:244-253`) updates `customers` and calls `engine.refresh_customer`. That method (`engine.py:106-116`) only rebuilds `signal_hits` and `twin`, so the cache is untouched.
- In `_guidance_items` (`api.py:278-290`), `intro` comes from the cache but `why` is recomputed live with `evidence_phrase(labels, lang)`. The two can therefore disagree.
- The voice endpoint reads the same cached `item["intro"]` (`api.py:312`), so the spoken text also keeps the stale wording.
- The web app reloads both twin and guidance after a toggle (`Mirror.tsx:31-41, 103-105`) and renders `item.intro` (`Mirror.tsx:235`). The stale sentence therefore appears in the guidance card directly beside the `dataNote` promise "Off means we don't read it at all" (`i18n.ts:32-33`).

Repro: I ran the real FastAPI app via TestClient on a freshly generated DB (seed 7, 4000 customers) in the scratchpad, logged in as sofie, and toggled consents.
- Initial state for buying_home is `ask`. The intro says "based on a transfer to a notary and a mortgage simulation in the app" and `why` is the same.
- After `app=false`, the belief is still `ask` at 0.64 with evidence only `['a transfer to a notary', 'your life stage']`. `why` becomes "a transfer to a notary", but the intro still says "...and a mortgage simulation in the app".
- After restoring `app=true` the texts agree again.
- With `transactions=false`, buying_home drops to `wait` and the guidance list is empty, so the contradiction only shows when the state stays ask/act/advisor. That is exactly Sofie's app-off case.
- The template text is what is cached here (`written_by: template`). The LLM path caches the same way.

Limits:
- The engine does stop reading the withdrawn data, so the README claim at line 135 still holds for what is read.
- The stale text is shown only to the same customer, so there is no cross-customer leak.
- The consent toggle is not in the README 3-minute demo script (README:99-107), as the reviewer says.
- I could not copy the live `mirror.duckdb` because it is locked by the running server, so I did not check whether it already holds stale cache rows.

Severity: medium is defensible. The defect is presentation-level but contradicts the product's consent and transparency pitch, and Sofie's app toggle is easy for a judge to try. Low would also be reasonable given the narrow trigger and the demo script not using it. The suggested fix is sound: delete the customer's cache rows in `refresh_customer`, or add an evidence hash to the key.

Reproduced. Code: message_cache is keyed by (customer_id, moment_id, state, lang, channel) (db.py:82-92; channels.py:128 and 120-125) with no evidence in the key. Channels.intro returns the cached row verbatim (channels.py:129-131) and writes it once (145-149). Nothing ever deletes from message_cache (grep: only db.py, channels.py). PUT /api/me/consents (api.py:244-253) only does UPDATE customers + engine.refresh_customer (engine.py:106-116), which rebuilds signal_hits and twin but not the cache. Consent is enforced in compile_hits (dsl.py:163), so the belief evidence does shrink. _guidance_items (api.py:269-293) then mixes the stale cached intro (line 279) with a live 'why' (line 290). Run: a scratch DB from the project's generator (the live duckdb is exclusively locked, so I generated a seed-42, 3000-customer DB; demo customers 1-3 are hand-written and identical) with a copy of the package that has no .env and blank LLM keys, driven through the real FastAPI endpoints via TestClient as sofie. Initial guidance for buying_home (ask): intro 'Hi Sofie, based on a transfer to a notary and a mortgage simulation in the app, we think this could be relevant for you. Are we right?'. After PUT /api/me/consents {transactions:true, app:false}: belief evidence is ['a transfer to a notary','your life stage'] at 0.64 (still ask) and why = 'a transfer to a notary', but intro is byte-identical and still names 'a mortgage simulation in the app'; the message_cache row still holds that text. Restoring consent returns the original text, so there is no other side effect. The reviewer's evidence is accurate. Extra scope the reviewer missed: (1) the voice channel (api.py:312 -> voice_script(item['intro'])) speaks the same stale text; (2) an LLM-written intro is also cached under the same key with the 'why' labels baked in (channels.py:132-141), so it would be stale too; (3) the cache lives in the DuckDB file and survives restarts; (4) only text that names evidence is visibly wrong: the 'ask' template embeds {evidence} (channels.py:26-28), while the 'act' and 'advisor' templates do not; (5) the growing_family card is unaffected in the repro because its signals are transaction-only. Fix is sound: DELETE FROM message_cache WHERE customer_id=$cid inside refresh_customer (already under db.lock) or an evidence hash in the key. Severity and demo impact: medium is fair as a correctness and trust bug, not high. It is not in the README 3-minute script (README.md:99-106 never toggles consent), it is only shown to the same customer, and there is no data leak to a third party. But the toggle sits on the same Mirror screen (Mirror.tsx:94-108), the UI re-fetches guidance after the toggle so the contradiction appears instantly on the headline Sofie card, and it directly contradicts the UI promise 'Off means we don't read it at all for suggestions' (i18n.ts:32-36) and the README claim 'switched-off data is never read' (README.md:135), a core pitch point for a privacy-by-design bank demo. It is a one-line fix, so worth doing before the demo.

findings.title: A template fallback is cached permanently, so AI intros never appear after a key is added or a call fails once
findings.detail: intro() tries Gemini, falls back to the template, and INSERT OR REPLACEs the result with source='template' (lines 141-149). Later calls return the cache hit (lines 128-130) and never retry Gemini. Practicing without a key, or one failed or timed-out Gemini call, pins template text for that customer/moment/state/language.
findings.evidence: v2_flow step 6: message_cache rows for customers 1,2,3 all source='template'. Code read at lines 120-150.
findings.fix: If you want to show 'Intro written by AI' on stage: set the key, reset the DB (or DELETE FROM message_cache with the API stopped), then open each demo customer once before the show. Code fix: do not cache fallbacks, or cache with a short TTL.
findings.demo_impact: Key added after practice -> no AI-written intro and no 'written by AI' tag; the 'the AI writes the words' claim stays invisible.

reasons:
I reproduced the behavior. The cited code is channels.py:127-150: a cache hit returns at 128-130 without calling Gemini, and any fallback is written with source='template' at 141-149 (INSERT OR REPLACE). Nothing ever evicts the row. The table (db.py:82-92) has a created_at column that is never read. The only DELETE statements in backend/mirror touch custom_moments, twin, signal_hits and feedback (engine.py:79-81,113-115; api.py:226), not message_cache. The key is (customer_id, moment_id, state, lang, channel), so it includes nothing about whether an LLM was available.

Repro: I copied backend/mirror and backend/moments into the scratchpad, so no .env was loaded, and generated a 1,500-customer DB there. `_gemini` returned None in step 1 and worked afterwards.
1. With no key, customer 2 got a 'template' intro.
2. After monkeypatching `_gemini` to return AI text, the same customer/moment/state/lang still returned the template.
3. A fresh Channels object on the same DB (equivalent to an API restart) still returned the template. The cache lives in the DuckDB file, so a restart does not clear it.
4. A different state (ask vs act) missed the cache and returned source='llm'.
5. A simulated transient Gemini failure for customer 1 was cached as template, and a recovered `_gemini` afterwards still returned the template.

The web UI only shows the "written by AI" note when `written_by === "llm"` (web/src/views/Mirror.tsx:271). A pinned template row therefore hides the AI claim, as the finding says.

Why it is not worse:
- It is cosmetic. Decisions come from the rules engine, and the template text is functionally fine.
- The README documents a clean reset ("stop the API and run the generator again", README.md:74). generate.py:317-320 deletes the .duckdb and .wal files, which wipes the cache.
- The README already says the Gemini path is untested with real keys and falls back to templates (README.md:142).
- Because `state` is in the key, the ask-to-act transition after Sofie confirms is a cache miss. A key added mid-demo would therefore still get one fresh Gemini call per new state, unless that state was already practiced.

Practical risk today: any failed or misconfigured Gemini test on Sofie, Lucas or Marc (for example a wrong model name) pins templates for those keys. After fixing the key or model, the AI intro would still not appear until the cache rows are deleted or the DB is regenerated.

I could not check the live DB's message_cache. The running server holds an exclusive lock, and both `cp` and a shared-read copy failed, so the claim that customers 1-3 all have source='template' is unverified by me. Whether a GEMINI_API_KEY is currently set is also unverified, since I did not read .env. The fix suggested in the finding is sound: either do not persist fallbacks, or do not serve cached rows whose source is 'template' when a key is configured.

Files: backend/mirror/channels.py, backend/mirror/db.py, backend/mirror/api.py (278-286), web/src/views/Mirror.tsx. Repro script: scratchpad/bk/repro.py.

The mechanism is real, but it is a pre-show ops trap with a cheap reset, not a medium demo risk.

What I checked:
- channels.py:127-150 is as described. A cache hit returns at 128-130 before any Gemini call. On a miss, _gemini() returns None when there is no key (70-71) or when the call fails (98-100). The template is then written with INSERT OR REPLACE and source='template' (141-149).
- The message_cache primary key is (customer_id, moment_id, state, lang, channel) (db.py:82-92). Only channels.py and db.py touch message_cache. Nothing in api.py or engine.py invalidates it on consent, feedback or refresh. There is no TTL, even though a created_at column exists (db.py:90).
- The UI shows the "Intro written by AI" tag only when written_by === "llm" (Mirror.tsx:271). A pinned template therefore removes the tag (web/src/i18n.ts:47).

Reproduction: scratch script /scratchpad/cf/repro.py, run against a fresh scratch DuckDB with the real Channels class and the real buying_home.yaml moment. The Gemini HTTP call is stubbed.
1. With no key, intro() for (customer 1, buying_home, ask, en) returned source=template.
2. With a key set and the stub returning a good answer, the same tuple returned source=template and made 0 HTTP calls. The fallback stayed pinned.
3. Control: a new tuple (state=act) returned source=llm after 1 HTTP call, so the stub works.
4. One simulated TimeoutError on (ask, nl) pinned a template. A retry after the stub recovered returned template with no new call.

Why I rate it low:
- Only tuples already opened before the key was set or before a failure stay pinned. The scripted flow in README:103-104 creates new tuples as it goes. Confirming moves Sofie from ask to act, which is a new key. Switching to NL is a new key. If you did not rehearse with the key unset, the AI intro and tag appear.
- Templates are valid, guardrailed text. The demo runs normally and the only loss is the "written by AI" tag.
- The fix is one line. Regenerating the DB deletes it and the WAL (generate.py:317-320, README:74). Stopping the API and running `DELETE FROM message_cache` also works.
- README:142 says the Gemini path has never been tested with real keys in this repo. That is a bigger demo risk than the caching.

The suggested code fix "do not cache fallbacks" has a cost. With a key set and Gemini down, every /api/me/guidance call, and every voice call that rebuilds the items, would block up to 15 s per item on the synchronous httpx.post (channels.py:94). The safer change is to skip the cache write only when no key is configured, or to give template rows a short TTL using the existing created_at column.

Not verified:
- The live DB is locked by the running server and I did not read `.env`, so I could not check whether a key is set or what message_cache holds there. The shell environment has none of GEMINI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT or ELEVENLABS_API_KEY.
- The only message_cache I read was a scratchpad replica, scratchpad/db/replica.duckdb. It holds 7 rows, all source='template', all for customer 1. The finding cites rows for customers 1, 2 and 3, which I did not see.

Files: backend/mirror/channels.py, backend/mirror/db.py, backend/mirror/generate.py and web/src/views/Mirror.tsx, all under the mirror project root.

findings.title: Deleting a custom moment leaves its feedback rows; re-adding resurrects them, and a stray EV chip click defers the growing_family card
findings.detail: delete_custom removes custom_moments, twin and signal_hits rows (lines 77-83) but not feedback. The fb CTE (dsl.py:206-207) picks feedback up again as soon as the moment id exists. Also, once EV is live Sofie's 'Tell us about a plan' chips include 'A new electric car'. Confirming it puts ev_purchase first in the fatigue ranking (dsl.py:233-240, confirmed first, MAX_ACTIVE=2) and pushes growing_family to deferred_fatigue, so the wrong-guess card vanishes from 'For you'.
findings.evidence: v6_misc.py T1c: Sofie clicks EV chip -> [('ev_purchase','act','confirmed'), ('buying_home','ask'), ('growing_family','deferred_fatigue')]. After DELETE + run the feedback row (1,'ev_purchase','confirmed') remains; after re-add Sofie has ev_purchase act/confirmed at once and EV reach is 435 instead of 434.
findings.fix: Reset the DB between rehearsal and show (summary). Code fix: DELETE FROM feedback WHERE moment_id=$id in delete_custom.
findings.demo_impact: After a rehearsal that removes and re-adds EV, Sofie (or anyone who clicked the EV chip) shows an EV plan that nobody asked for.

reasons:
The defect is real, but the stated demo impact is overstated, so I rate it low rather than medium.

**What I reproduced.** I ran a scratch script, `refute_fb/t.py` in the scratchpad. It builds a fresh 4000-customer DB and drives the real FastAPI app through TestClient. I could not use the live DB because it is locked.
- `engine.py:75-83` (`delete_custom`) deletes from `custom_moments`, `twin` and `signal_hits`, but never from `feedback`. After DELETE, the `feedback` row `(1, ev_purchase, confirmed)` was still there.
- While the moment is deleted, the leftover row is inert. The `fb` CTE at `dsl.py:206-207` filters on `moment_id IN (SELECT moment_id FROM moments_rt)`, and Sofie's twin and guidance showed no EV.
- After re-adding EV and running, Sofie had `ev_purchase` as `act` with no behavioural evidence. EV reach went from 12 to 13. The finding's 434 to 435 is the same +1 on a different dataset.
- Once EV is live, `_twin_payload` (`api.py:197-198`) offers it as a chip, "A new electric car". Confirming it gave `[buying_home ask, ev_purchase act, growing_family deferred_fatigue]`, and guidance dropped `growing_family`. This matches `dsl.py:233-240`, which ranks confirmed items first, with `MAX_ACTIVE=2` at `config.py:42`.

**Why it is overstated.**
- **Not on the scripted path.** The README demo script (lines 99-107) has Sofie at 0:50 and adds EV at 2:15. EV is not live during Sofie's segment, so no EV chip exists. Sofie rejects `growing_family` in that segment anyway, so it vanishing is expected.
- **Needs an unscripted sequence.** Someone has to leave EV live, click the EV chip as a customer, delete EV, and re-add it without resetting. The README documents the reset at line 74 ("stop the API and run the generator again").
- **Deferral is by design.** The "stray click defers `growing_family`" part is the confirmed-first ranking working as coded. The customer did click the chip, so "nobody asked for it" is not quite right.
- **Stale state self-heals in the UI.** My raw API delete, with no run, left `growing_family` as `deferred_fatigue` (the twin is not recomputed on delete). But `ProductOwner.tsx:60-66` calls `run()` after every delete, which recomputes all customers, so the UI path does not show this.
- **Effect is small.** It amounts to one extra card for a customer who previously confirmed it, plus +1 reach on the EV row.

The one-line fix in `delete_custom` is still worth making: `DELETE FROM feedback WHERE moment_id = $id`. Otherwise, reset the DB before the show.

Files:
- `C:/Users/Dario/OneDrive - Erasmushogeschool Brussel/Hackathon/Tectronic_30.09.2026/mirror/backend/mirror/engine.py`
- `C:/Users/Dario/OneDrive - Erasmushogeschool Brussel/Hackathon/Tectronic_30.09.2026/mirror/backend/mirror/dsl.py`
- `C:/Users/Dario/OneDrive - Erasmushogeschool Brussel/Hackathon/Tectronic_30.09.2026/mirror/backend/mirror/api.py`

The mechanics are real and I reproduced them, but the demo impact is overstated, so I rate it low rather than medium.

**Caveat on method.** The live mirror.duckdb and its .wal are exclusively locked by the running server. Both Copy-Item and a FileShare.ReadWrite open failed, so I could not inspect the live DB's feedback or custom_moments rows. Instead I generated a fresh 100k seed-42 DB in the scratchpad with the project's generator. I then drove the real API through TestClient (scripts: scratchpad/v6/repro.py and undo.py). Nothing in the project root was touched.

**Code confirmed.**
- engine.py:75-83, `delete_custom`, deletes custom_moments, twin and signal_hits rows, but never feedback.
- dsl.py:206-207: the `fb` CTE filters on `moment_id IN (SELECT moment_id FROM moments_rt)`.
  - While EV is deleted, its stale feedback is filtered out and dormant.
  - It revives as soon as the id is re-added.

**Reproduced, as the reviewer described.**
1. After adding EV, the run gives EV reach 434.
2. Sofie clicks the "A new electric car" chip. This goes through api.py:218-235 and web Mirror.tsx:83. Her For-you becomes [ev_purchase act, buying_home ask], and growing_family becomes deferred_fatigue (rank by `confirmed` first at dsl.py:236, MAX_ACTIVE=2).
3. DELETE EV and run: the feedback table still holds {customer_id 1, ev_purchase, confirmed}, while Sofie's view returns to [buying_home ask, growing_family ask].
4. Re-add EV and run, with no click: reach is 435, and Sofie again shows ev_purchase act/confirmed with growing_family deferred_fatigue.

**Why I downgrade the severity.**
- **Precondition.** The reviewer's own chain needs a customer to click the EV chip, or answer an EV ask, between a rehearsal add and the delete. That is then followed by a re-add of the same id.
- **Scripted demo.** README.md:100-110 never returns to Sofie after EV goes live: Sofie is step 3 at 0:50, and EV is added at step 5 (2:15). Nothing in the scripted flow triggers this.
- **Part of the claim is by design.** Sofie's chip click deferring growing_family is the intended "confirmed first" fatigue policy (dsl.py:233-240), not a bug. Only the persistence after delete is a real defect.
- **Documented reset already avoids it.** README.md:68 says to regenerate a clean demo state. generate.py:~315-319 unlinks both the .duckdb and the .wal, so feedback and custom_moments are wiped.
- **Rehearsal contamination is broader than this.** A rehearsal where Sofie rejects growing_family (demo step 3) already breaks the demo and needs the same reset.
- **One-click recovery.** After the stale row revives, the EV belief card shows Undo (Mirror.tsx:181). Clearing it restored Sofie to [buying_home ask, growing_family ask], and the EV chip returned. I ran this in undo.py, and EV reach went back to 434.
- **PO numbers barely move.** The EV precision and recall figures are untouched: stats use `inferred >= ask_t` and feedback-only rows have inferred 0. Only reach/act shifts by one, and README does not quote reach.

**Verdict.** It is a valid but minor orphaned-data bug. The one-line fix is to also run `DELETE FROM feedback WHERE moment_id=$id` in `delete_custom`. The practical mitigation is to regenerate the DB before the live show.
